page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E3.Flex.64-1024 is a high-capacity flexible virtual machine instance powered by second-generation AMD EPYC processors. Configured with 64 dedicated physical cores (128 vCPUs via two threads per core) operating at a base frequency of 2.25 GHz on the x86_64 AMD EPYC 7742 architecture, this instance allocates 1024.0 GB of system memory. This yields a dense 8.0 GB of memory per core ratio, prioritizing workloads requiring large memory capacities alongside significant parallel compute capability.

Hardware capabilities do not include local NVMe or SSD storage, requiring reliance on remote block storage volumes for persistent data retention. It operates without dedicated GPU acceleration, relying strictly on CPU resources for compute operations. The instance also includes one complimentary public IPv4 address for external network access.

The 1:8 core-to-RAM ratio positions this instance as an efficient resource allocation for high-density enterprise software. It eliminates the cost of idle hardware accelerators while providing a massive 1 TB memory pool. Suitable production workloads include in-memory databases, large-scale distributed analytics, high-density container virtualization, memory-heavy ETL processing, and large enterprise applications needing substantial memory footprints without discrete GPUs.

The extensive memory footprint coupled with high core count makes VM.Standard.E3.Flex.64-1024 suited for memory-intensive enterprise environments, in-memory database deployments, big data caching, and large-scale parallel processing jobs.
